text.p: The deadline for expressions of interest in Bermuda-based tanker operator London & Overseas Freighters Plc Limited was set to pass today.

LOFS chief financial officer Huw Spiers declined to comment on the response the company had received but said: "Deadlines are movable things. A lot depends on who or what comes forward, but things could move quickly."
Earlier LOFS has said: "The enhancement of shareholder value in the company will be the primary objective."

In February 1997, LOFS appointed Gleacher NatWest Inc and NatWest Securities Limited as financial advisers and said it was "exploring a range of strategic alternatives aimed at positioning itself to compete more effectively in the changing market for quoted tanker companies."
Analysts took the LOFS plan to mean the company recognised it was too small and was looking for a merger or sale.

Some analysts said they thought a couple of London Greek owners were taking an interest as well as at least one Norwegian owner, thought possibly to be John Fredriksen. No one was available for comment at John Fredriksen.
LOFS operates a fleet of three Suezmax and three Panamax tankers under the British flag. It values its fleet at $219.8 million.
The company reported a net profit of $596,000 for the third quarter ending December 31, 1996, compared with $29,000 for the same period the year before.
But it said then that net operating income for its Panamax fleet decreased by $53,000 to $427,000 and added that it felt its profit levels "remained disappointing".

In December 1996, LOFS put into place a shareholders' rights plan "designed to enhance the board's ability to protect shareholders against ... unsolicited attempts to acquire control of LOFS that do not offer an adequate price to all shareholders."
The company has since expressed optimism that it can benefit from improving tanker markets, particularly with its Suezmax vessels whose earnings improved in the third quarter.
